structural_duplicates.field_definition: Residual counts after the Pedant Evidence Contract filter and disposition, not raw tool output: the contract states the structural-duplicate output is a candidate set, not a zero-result gate. changed_exact_groups counts exact subgroups with two or more plan-written functions that survive DRY review as genuine duplicated logic. unresolved_responsibility_candidates counts same-responsibility structural candidates among plan-written functions with no recorded disposition.
structural_duplicates.exact_hash_semantics: Pedant's exact_hash is normalized over identifiers and literals, so it groups functions identical up to renaming. Two distinct-responsibility one-expression builder setters collide under it. Raw equality with zero is therefore unattainable for any validated builder vocabulary; the raw inventory is recorded in full below.
structural_duplicates.missing_file_filter: The MCP index returned eight facts from one editor temporary file that does not exist in the audited tree. Raw counts retain those facts. Candidate review excludes them because a nonexistent path cannot be plan-written source or a duplicate implementation.
structural_duplicates.plan_written_test: no function of that name existed in that file at plan_base_sha

candidates.rationale: Distinct constant constructors at two ownership levels. ServerPolicy::of assembles the whole server envelope and delegates its request defaults to RequestBudget::from_constants; sharing their remaining field writes would merge the server policy with the request budget it contains.

Two implementations of one generic worker-observation trait route distinct event vocabularies to their corresponding LifecycleScript sink. The shared worker protocol is already generic over the trait; only the required per-type sink selection remains in each impl.

Distinct validated builder setters: each writes one distinct field on one type and delegates its validation to the single shared owner (finite_duration, positive_limit, clamped_duration). The shared logic is already extracted; what collides is the one-line field write and its own published Rustdoc contract.
Display over distinct closed types, each rendering its own vocabulary through its own label owner. A shared impl cannot name two vocabularies.
